doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Origin of The Real Ambassadors after the State Department tour
summary: Iola explains the musical grew from the 1958 State Department tour, jazz as a symbol of freedom in Poland, and Louis Armstrong's commitment.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When it came time to work on the religious pieces, and you guys worked together with the text from the Bible very often.
But the first things that you did with him, they were more of a secular nature, like “The Real Ambassadors.”
When did that come about? Thinking like I can do this with him.
Yeah, I guess, but I’m just wondering if there was a point where you said you know what, I think I can make a contribution lyrically?

Well it sort of grew. The idea for “The Real Ambassadors” really came after they did the State Department tour. And I was so impressed with how jazz and music was received in cultures that were different from ours, and what it actually meant at that period in that part of the world. In Poland, for example, jazz just became this symbol of the freedom that they wanted and were seeking. And so it was an underground movement that for some time was forbidden, and by the time, in 1958, when the quartet went there, it had loosened up a little bit so there could be jazz societies. But it was still very suspect. And just from my observations I thought this is something that is not being expressed to the American public as a whole. They knew about the going overseas, the musicians, and as far as the American public is concerned they’re just entertaining. But they’re not just entertaining. There’s something deeper going on. So that was what started it. And then,

how do you express that? How do you get that idea over to the public? Then I decided one way perhaps would be to put it into a musical so that you would have jazz musicians on the stage. I love the sense of humor and I thought if you could just capture some of that, it would be so great, and the public would like it. So that’s how it came about, and then getting to Louis Armstrong and talking to him, and much to our surprise he really took it very, very seriously and really wanted to do it. And it’s interesting I read a story by Leonard Feather when I was just — fairly recently I read it because I was going through old papers and stuff, where he had interviewed Armstrong in Sweden I think it was, and he was asked what he was interested in doing and he said something about “The Real Ambassadors” and saying that that was something that he hoped he could do because he said it really had meaning for him.
